part_1_why_epoch_2_is_necessary.epoch_1_topology: the registered contract requires the epoch-1 implementation commit to be the direct single-parent child of the preregistration commit be64235
part_1_why_epoch_2_is_necessary.real_history: be64235 was followed by cf10ef8, which independent review BLOCKED, then by the remediation fae44154 whose parent is cf10ef8, approved and landed by merge be7a2ce. No commit satisfying the epoch-1 rule can exist for the approved bytes: rebinding to cf10ef8 fails require_current because the working bytes are fae44154's, and fae44154 itself is not a direct child of be64235 and is not an ancestor of the review commit 16f3e70.
part_1_why_epoch_2_is_necessary.conclusion: The epoch-1 rule encodes an idealized straight-line history. The actual history was bent by a blocker and its remediation, which is the governance process working, not a defect. The contract's own escape is a later epoch, and it is used here rather than any relaxation of the epoch-1 rule.
